framework: National Curriculum of Pakistan 2026 (Commerce Group, Grades 11-12)
subject: Trade and Commerce

source.publisher: National Curriculum Council, Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training
source.licence: Government publication; structure + our own wording only

outcomes.text: Define home and international trade and name their main types: wholesale, retail, import, export, entrepot.
Explain how home and international trade differ and the barriers to the latter: tariffs, quotas, paperwork.
Name the key trade documents: invoice, bill of lading, letter of credit, bill of exchange.
Put trade documents in the right order for an import or export, showing each one's role.
Work out the landed cost of goods from price, freight, insurance and customs duty.
Describe the balance of trade and balance of payments and why they matter for Pakistan.
Describe the standard operating procedures for a domestic and an international trade deal.
Draw a flow diagram of an international trade deal from order to delivery and payment.

subtopics.title: Trade policy and entering international trade

outcomes.text: Analyse how a new tariff or import restriction affects a Pakistani importer or exporter.
Evaluate whether a business should enter international trade, weighing chances against risks.
Name the aids to trade (communication, transport, warehousing, advertising, banking, insurance) and their purpose.
Explain how communication and advertising promote trade and reach customers.
Describe transport functions and what to weigh when choosing road, rail, sea or air.
Compare transport modes on cost, speed, safety and fit for goods.
Describe types and jobs of warehouses: storing goods, steadying supply, adding time utility.
Explain how banks help trade: trade finance, letters of credit, guarantees, collections, remittances, foreign exchange.
Explain how insurance manages trade risk: marine, cargo, fire insurance and the principle of indemnity.
Pick suitable transport, storage and payment methods for a trading scenario.
Calculate transport or warehousing cost for a consignment and recommend the cheapest option.
Analyse how the aids to trade work together in one import or export deal.

subtopics.title: Judging the key aid and payment method

outcomes.text: Judge which aid to trade matters most for a given business and justify it.
Judge the best payment method for an exporter (letter of credit, advance, open account), weighing risk and cost.

units.title: Domain C: Commerce and Digital Commerce

outcomes.text: Define commerce and its parts: trade and aids to trade.
Name the forms of digital commerce (e-, m- and s-commerce) with examples.
Explain the features of e-, m- and s-commerce with Pakistani platform examples.
Explain how digital payments like JazzCash, Easypaisa and Raast affect trade.
Explain the impact of AI on commerce: chatbots, recommendations, logistics automation, forecasting, plus ethical and job issues.
Outline how a small trader goes online, from platform choice to payment and delivery.
Compare traditional and digital commerce on cost, reach, convenience and scope.
Evaluate benefits and risks of e-commerce for a small Pakistani business.
Develop a simple digital-commerce plan for a product.

units.title: Domain D: Commercial Operations and Enterprise

outcomes.text: Name the forms of commercial operation: public and private enterprises, MNCs, franchises.
Tell public from private enterprises by ownership and objectives.
Explain the features and economic role of MNCs and franchises.
Compare forms of commercial operation for a business context.
Describe outsourcing, retailing and wholesaling and where they fit in distribution.
Explain the supply chain and flow of goods from producer to consumer.
Map a product's path from producer through wholesaler and retailer to consumer.
Analyse pros and cons of franchising for franchisor and franchisee.
Evaluate whether to expand by franchise or own outlets and justify it.

subtopics.title: Types, methods and barriers of communication

outcomes.text: Classify business communication: written, oral, electronic, visual.
Describe methods: letters, phone, meetings, email, video calls, chat, social media, posters.
Explain barriers to good business communication and how to overcome them.
Explain strengths and limits of each method.
Prepare a business letter, email or notice for a trade situation.
Analyse which method best suits a message and audience.
Select and justify the best method for a commercial scenario.
Design a short communication plan for a business event or campaign.

units.title: Domain F: Ethics and Consumer Protection in Commerce

outcomes.text: Define business ethics and common issues: fraud, corruption, hoarding, unfair practices.
Explain the effects of unethical trade on businesses, consumers and society.
Apply ethical principles to a dilemma and pick the responsible action.
Analyse a case of unfair trade practice and its effect on stakeholders.
Describe basic consumer rights and why consumer protection matters in Pakistan.
Explain corporate social responsibility in commerce.
Evaluate ways a business can promote ethics and protect consumers.
Develop a simple code of ethics or consumer charter for a small trading business.

units.title: Domain G: Legal Foundations of Trade and Commerce

outcomes.text: Name the main trade laws: Contract Act 1872, Sale of Goods Act 1930, Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, Income Tax Ordinance 2001, Sales Tax Act 1990.
Explain contract, agreement, offer, acceptance, consideration and enforceability under the Contract Act.
Apply the essentials of a valid contract to a scenario to decide if it binds.
Explain contract of sale, sale, agreement to sell, conditions and warranties.
Analyse a sale-of-goods dispute to see if a condition or warranty was breached.
Define promissory note, bill of exchange and cheque, and kinds of cheques: open and crossed.
Complete or read a specimen crossed cheque or bill of exchange.
Judge the best negotiable instrument or safeguard for a transaction.
Explain filer, non-filer, tax year, taxable income and income-tax return.
Explain output tax, input tax, taxable, exempt and zero-rated supplies.
Calculate sales tax payable from input and output tax.
